title: With Castile beaten in the field and its army besieging Valladolid, the Emperor turns on the Portuguese, who have come down on Ishbīliya. At Shalūqa al-Kubrā on the city's outskirts he meets them, 10,300 against 11,300, and throws them back across the border: 8,343 of theirs lost for 1,069 of ours

data.location: Sanlúcar la Mayor (Šaluqa el-Kubra), by Seville

source: Trent's account and battle screens, 7–17 January 1378

title: The Emperor's mother Sayyida turns from promoting Andalusī culture to the realm's diplomatic endeavours

Peace with Castile and Portugal. Valladolid is weeks from falling, the Emperor's army is marching on Lisbon, the Moors have cleared a path through the sea, and the first Mamlūk army is off the coast of Tunis. Offered the choice the Aragonese were given, peace or blood, the Iberians choose peace. The Aragonese heartland, 24 towns from Jaca to Teruel with Zaragoza at its heart, is restored to the renewed Kingdom of Aragon; 46 towns of the Middle and Lower Marches, Toledo, Badajoz and Mérida among them, pass to al-Andalus; Castile pays reparations. The war score stands at +100%. The castles of León, Zamora, Valladolid, Segovia, Cuenca, Pamplona and Laguardia, in the lands Castile keeps, are to be razed

data.truces: with Castile, Portugal, the Papal States and its vassals to 6 April 1393

battleDead.note: losses in the war's land battles from the save's battle list, ours with the ṭāʾifas; attrition and sieges not counted

data.alsoGone: in the ceded towns the military orders' commanderies at Consuegra and Alcázar de San Juan and six rotten boroughs vanished with the change of owner

title: By the peace Castile razes seven of its castles in the lands it keeps, opening the road to its heart: León, Zamora, Valladolid, Segovia, Cuenca, Pamplona and Laguardia
source: saves of 6 April 1378 before and after the peace (buildings compared); Trent's account

title: The Gem of Iberia. Ṭulayṭula, at the centre of Iberia and long a meeting place of Christian, Muslim and Jewish cultures, is in the Emperor's hands, and the court and all the estates set out to make it the gem of Iberia. The city gains half a point of development and 30% prosperity, and it and the towns of its land become cores of al-Andalus

cores: and others below the fold of Trent's screen

source: Trent's screenshot of the event, 1 May 1378

title: The first new office of the expanded bureaucracy: the Count of the Christians, the qūmis of the caliphs' Córdoba, to administer and integrate the conquered Christian lands. As long as the crown pays for it, it raises tax efficiency and tolerance and keeps the dhimmīs content without costing the ʿulamāʾ their patience or slowing conversion

data.precedent: the qūmis of the Christians of Córdoba, with a Christian judge under Visigothic law and a head of the Jews such as Ḥasdai ibn Shaprūṭ under ʿAbd al-Raḥmān III (the game's text)
data.note: the negative effects apply only when the bureaucracy is unfunded, the positive only when it is funded (Trent)

title: With Castile's gold, the Emperor expands the famed silk of Gharnāṭa into Mursiyya, now in the crown's own hands, to export still more of it to the rest of Europe: 500 from the treasury for a permanent rise in Murcia's silk

murcia.lasts: until the land ceases to be

source: Trent's account and screenshot of the decision, spring 1378

title: As part of the integration of the new lands, and beside the Count of the Christians, a governor is placed in Ṭulayṭula

The scholars of the realm work toward Khilāfat Qurṭuba Renewed: the ceremonial of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān III revived, the throne hall of a rebuilt Madīnat al-Zahrāʾ, ṭirāz robes worked in gold thread with the ruler's regnal year, the Friday sermon in the Great Mosque of Qurṭuba, dīnārs of West African gold, investiture banners for the Maghribī sultans, and the Mamlūks received as equals; the dhimma covenant over the realm's Christians and Jews formalised

data.note: part of the reforms and the integration of the new lands (Trent); the step toward the caliphate the Emperor may one day claim
